title: The Social Engineer
author: Barış Kısır
short_description: An elite con artist hired to infiltrate a data-broker conglomerate discovers her own psychological file in its system — and must run the greatest con of her life on the people who wrote the playbook.
long_description:
Alex Mercer steals secrets, not money. Pretexting, phishing, tailgating, impersonation — she can become anyone for eleven minutes or eleven weeks, and no one has ever caught her. When a mysterious client hires her to infiltrate Helix Dyne, a data-broker conglomerate with profiles on 280 million people, she expects a routine job. Instead she finds a machine that sells fear as a product and elections as a deliverable — and her own file in the archive, more accurate than her memories, built from the one job she buried years ago.

The client, it turns out, was never hers: the whole job was an audit commissioned by Helix's reclusive founder, Silas Crane, the one man on Earth the machine refuses to profile. Her story is published and buried in a day, her handler has sold a piece of her, and her own team may be turned. So Alex does the one thing the file can never predict: she becomes exactly what it forecasts — a contained, converted asset — walks back through the front door, and begins the longest performance of her life.

From the badge readers of Helix's lobby to a windowless boardroom in Zurich, The Social Engineer is a sharp, witty caper-thriller about the last person alive who can read a room — and the con she runs on the people who wrote the playbook, armed with nothing but paper, a rotary press, and the machine's one blind spot: it can model what you fear, but it can't model you changing.
